paper.title: Localized exploration in contextual dynamic pricing achieves dimension-free regret

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual dynamic pricing with a linear demand model
unmapped: Action is a continuous price p in a known interval [l,u]; demand D_t = x_t^T alpha* + p_t (x_t^T beta*) + eps_t, revenue p*E[D] quadratic in price
Contexts i.i.d. sub-Gaussian with well-conditioned second-moment matrix (Assumption 1)
Optimal price bounded away from interval boundary; intercept and slope of constant order (Assumption 2)
Learner knows the feasible price range [l,u]
settings.definition_quote: D_t = x_t^T alpha* + p_t (x_t^T beta*) + eps_t. Here eps_t represents random demand shocks, which are assumed to be sub-Gaussian with zero mean and a variance proxy of sigma^2 > 0 ... R(T) = sum_{t=1}^T { r*(x_t) - r_t }.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear dynamic pricing, deterministic contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: Contexts x_1..x_T are deterministic (fixed), with ||x_t||_2 <= C_f sqrt(d); regret conditional on x_{1:T}
Parameter class M_{b1,b2,rho1,rho2}: intercepts/slopes in [b1,b2], norms bounded below, non-collinear
settings.definition_quote: For deterministic x_1,...,x_T in X such that ||x_t||_2 <= C_f sqrt(d) ... inf_pi sup_{theta in M} E[ sum_t ( r*(x_t;theta) - r(x_t,p_t;theta) ) | x_{1:T} ] >~ sqrt(T).

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear dynamic pricing, i.i.d. contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: Contexts i.i.d. satisfying Assumptions 1 and 3 (sub-Gaussian, well-conditioned, anti-concentration)
settings.definition_quote: For x_t ~ mu satisfying Assumptions 1 and 3, we have inf_pi sup_{theta in M} E[R(T;theta)] >~ sqrt(T).

conditions: Assumptions 1, 2, 3 (sub-Gaussian well-conditioned contexts, optimal price interior with constant-order intercept/slope, anti-concentration and non-collinearity of alpha*, beta*)

source.quote: If the planning horizon T is sufficiently large, satisfying T >= C_1 d^4 log^2 T and the hyperparameters are set according to ..., then Algorithm 1 achieves ... (a) With probability at least 1 - c T^{-2}, the cumulative regret is bounded by R(T) <= C { sqrt(T) log T + eta^2 T / d }.

results.notes: With eta ≍ sqrt((d/sqrt T) log T), the bound becomes C sqrt(T) log T (dimension-free), stated in text after the theorem. Regret is defined via expected revenue given chosen price against per-context optimal price.
